Having a consistent practice of turning to the **Quran and Hadith**—especially in moments of difficulty or decision-making—can profoundly shape how someone determines what is **right, just, and aligned with their faith**. Anchors Decision-Making in Divine Guidance** - The Quran and Hadith serve as **eternal, unchanging sources of wisdom** that transcend personal biases, emotions, or societal pressures. I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved. Strike [them] over the necks and strike over every finger of them.'" (Quran 8:12) *(This teaches patience and wisdom in conflict.)* ### **4. Reduces Emotional Reactivity** - When you’re **stressed, angry, or fearful**, your emotions can cloud judgment. Builds Consistency and Integrity** - Over time, this practice **shapes your character** (*akhlaq*). Encourages Community and Accountability** - When you **consult the Quran and Hadith**, you’re often also engaging with **scholars, family, or the ummah** (Muslim community) for guidance.
